title: Israeli Defense Minister Calls Erdoğan a 'Paper Sultan'; Turkey Rebukes
detail: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz called President Erdoğan a 'paper sultan' who should 'stop messing with Israel,' accusing him of financing and embracing Hamas and of dreaming of restoring the Ottoman Empire while failing to back Saudi Arabia against Houthi missile attacks despite a defense pact. Turkey's presidential communications directorate rebuked the remarks, which came after Erdoğan's September 22 UN speech branding Gaza a 'concentration camp.'

media.caption: Turkey rebukes Israeli Defense Minister Katz's 'paper sultan' remarks about Erdoğan

title: Magnitude 5.4 Earthquake Strikes Şanlıurfa, No Casualties Reported
detail: An earthquake measured at magnitude 5.4 by Turkey's AFAD (5.1 per EMSC; revised to 5.5 by Kandilli Observatory) struck the Karaköprü district of Şanlıurfa in southeastern Turkey at 10:40 a.m. local time at a depth of roughly 5–7 km. Tremors were felt across Diyarbakır, Mardin, Siirt, Şırnak, Batman, Gaziantep, Adıyaman and Malatya provinces. Şanlıurfa's governor reported no deaths, injuries or building collapses; about 40 people sought treatment for panic-related symptoms, and schools were closed as a precaution against aftershocks.

media.caption: Magnitude 5.4 earthquake shakes Şanlıurfa; no casualties reported

title: EBRD Cuts Turkey's 2026 Growth Forecast to 3%
detail: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development lowered its 2026 growth forecast for Turkey to 3.0% from 3.5% in its latest Regional Economic Prospects report, citing weaker domestic demand amid high inflation, tight financial conditions and the impact of the Middle East conflict on energy prices, tourism and trade. The bank projected growth would accelerate to 4.0% in 2027 if regional tensions ease; the downgrade follows similar cuts by the OECD (3.1%), IMF (2.9%) and World Bank (2.8%).

media.caption: EBRD cuts Turkey's 2026 growth outlook to 3%, citing inflation and regional conflict
